title: Perceptual Evaluations: Evals for Aesthetics — Diego Rodriguez, Krea.ai
talk_summary: A philosophical talk from Krea.ai's co-founder arguing that standard generative-media metrics (FID, CLIP adherence) fail to capture human perception and aesthetics, and that evals should be trained to encode human opinion rather than easy-to-measure proxies. It offers almost no concrete engineering mechanism beyond 'train a classifier on human-labeled good examples'.

takeaways.technique: Train a learned judge on labeled examples instead of relying on proxy metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that when the quality signal is subjective, you should train a classifier on sets of examples humans have labeled as good, rather than using off-the-shelf metrics that are sensitive to irrelevant artifacts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can train so that it understands what we mean and it's like hey I show you these five images these five images are actually all good

takeaways.technique: Beware metrics that react to irrelevant artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: Shows FID scores collapsing on JPEG-artifacted images that are perceptually identical, warning that metrics can measure the wrong thing and mislead model selection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you start adding JPEG artifacts and the score is like oh no no no this is horrible horrible image
